passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a new dietary supplement on endurance performance in trained cyclists. Thirty male cyclists, aged 20–35, were randomly assigned to a control group (n=15) receiving a placebo or an experimental group (n=15) receiving the supplement. After an 8‑week training program, participants completed a 30‑km time trial. Key performance metrics were recorded: average speed (km/h), VO₂ max (ml·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹), and blood lactate concentration (mmol/L) immediately post‑trial. The supplement group showed a mean average speed of 45.2 ± 2.1 km/h versus 42.8 ± 2.4 km/h in the control group. VO₂ max was 58.7 ± 3.5 ml·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹ in the supplement group versus 55.3 ± 3.2 in the control group, and post-trial lactate concentration was 7.8 ± 0.7 mmol/L versus 8.5 ± 0.9 in the control group. The authors concluded that the supplement significantly improved endurance performance, likely through enhanced aerobic capacity and delayed lactate accumulation.
stem: Which performance metric showed the greatest relative improvement in the supplement group compared to the control group?
explanation: Correct: Relative differences versus control are speed +5.6% (45.2 vs 42.8), VO₂ max +6.1% (58.7 vs 55.3) and blood lactate −8.2% (7.8 vs 8.5); a lower lactate is an improvement, and 8.2% is the largest. Why the others are wrong: A) average speed improved by only 5.6%. B) VO₂ max improved by 6.1%, less than the 8.2% lactate change. D) the three relative changes are 5.6%, 6.1% and 8.2%, so they are not equal.
trap: Choosing speed or VO₂ max because both rose, without converting the lactate decrease into a percent change (−8.2%).

stem: Which feature of the described design allows a difference between groups to be attributed to the supplement rather than to pre-existing differences among cyclists?

options.A: Random assignment of the cyclists to the control or supplement group
options.B: Measuring VO₂ max in both groups
options.C: Reporting a standard deviation for each mean
options.D: Using a 30-km distance for the time trial

explanation: Correct: Random assignment distributes known and unknown cyclist characteristics across the groups by chance, so group differences can be attributed to the supplement. Why the others are wrong: B) measuring the same variable in both groups shows the outcome but does not make the groups comparable at the start. C) a standard deviation describes spread within a group and does not affect who is in which group. D) the same trial distance for everyone standardizes the test but does not address pre-existing differences between groups.
trap: Treating standardized measurement or reporting SDs as if they controlled for differences between groups; only random assignment does that.

stem: What is the percent increase in VO₂ max for the supplement group relative to the control group?
explanation: Correct: Percent increase = (58.7 − 55.3)/55.3 × 100 = 3.4/55.3 × 100 ≈ 6.1%. Why the others are wrong: A) 3.2% is not obtained from the VO₂ max means. B) 5.6% is the percent increase in average speed (2.4/42.8), not in VO₂ max. D) 8.4% is not obtained from these values; the 8.2% lactate change is a decrease in a different variable.
trap: Using the speed percent change (5.6%) or the lactate change (8.2%) instead of the VO₂ max change (6.1%).

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data?

options.A: The supplement group had a higher mean average speed than the control group
options.B: The supplement group had a higher mean VO2 max than the control group
options.C: The supplement group had lower post-trial blood lactate than the control group
options.D: Table 1 alone demonstrates that enhanced aerobic capacity is the mechanism of the speed gain

explanation: Correct: Table 1 reports group means for speed, VO2 max and lactate; it contains no mediation analysis, and the passage only says the mechanism is likely. Why the others are wrong: A) 45.2 versus 42.8 km/h, so this is supported. B) 58.7 versus 55.3 ml/kg/min, so this is supported. C) 7.8 versus 8.5 mmol/L, so this is supported.
trap: Reading parallel differences in several measures as proof of the cause of the improvement.

stem: How do the findings of this study link to the broader field of sports nutrition?

options.A: They support the role of targeted supplementation in enhancing aerobic capacity.
options.B: They refute the importance of training intensity in performance gains.
options.C: They demonstrate that supplements replace the need for adequate hydration.
options.D: They indicate that performance improvements are solely due to placebo effects.

explanation: Correct: A supplement group with higher VO₂ max and lower lactate than a placebo group is consistent with targeted supplementation raising aerobic capacity. Why the others are wrong: B) the study did not vary training intensity, so it cannot refute its importance. C) hydration was not tested, so nothing can be concluded about replacing it. D) a placebo group was included, and the supplement group outperformed it, so the improvement is not attributable to placebo alone.
trap: Over-reading a single trial as refuting other training factors or as showing a placebo effect, despite the placebo control group.
